description: Per-consumer usage and quota. Balance comes from the durable ai-quota ledger via redis_exporter; rates from Higress ai-statistics; per-consumer latency and status mix from the access-log fact table via Vector. Billing reads the ledger, never the counters.

list.name: consumer
list.label: Consumer
list.description: Roster comes from the quota ledger, not from traffic: a key created a minute ago has a balance and no requests yet, and the access-log counters vanish from Prometheus entirely while the node is idle. All = .* rather than the OR of this list, so traffic from a consumer that is not in the ledger (or unauthenticated) still shows up instead of silently disappearing.

list.name: window
list.label: Window
list.description: Window for the exact per-consumer tables: the preceding 1h, 24h, 7d or 30d, independent of the time picker.

title: Usage & Quota

panels.title: Consumer ledger
panels.description: Balance is the DURABLE record and is a single TOTAL-token number: ai-quota deducts input+output at the same rate and v2.2.4 has no weighting option. The in/out columns show what that total was actually made of — output tokens each cost a forward pass, while input is prefilled once and mostly radix-cache served. Spend and share come from Envoy counters, which reset on gateway restart and must never be invoiced.

panels.title: Ledger reachable
panels.description: redis_up for higress-redis. Not a nicety: ai-quota has no fail-open, so if the ledger is unreachable every billable route returns 403 'No quota left' regardless of actual balances — indistinguishable, to a caller, from having run out.

panels.title: Funded consumers
panels.description: Consumers holding a chat_quota key. A revoked consumer's key is deleted, so this is the live count.

panels.title: Balance by consumer
panels.description: Remaining tokens, straight from the ledger.

panels.title: Token rate by consumer, split by direction
panels.description: Token throughput per consumer from SGLang's own counters, for the shape over time. For totals use 'Exact usage by consumer' — rate() here is fine for a trend but increase() over these counters loses the first request after a replica restart. Input and output are charged identically, but an output token is a forward pass and input on an agent re-sending its context is mostly a prefix-cache hit.

panels.title: Request rate by consumer
panels.description: Requests finished per second, per consumer, as SGLang counts them.

panels.title: Mean time to first token (engine), by consumer
panels.description: Mean TTFT as SGLang measured it (queue wait + prefill). A MEAN: one slow request among a hundred fast ones barely moves it — the p95 panels show the tail.

panels.title: Share of node (1h)
panels.description: Each consumer's tokens as a fraction of everything the ENGINE produced and consumed, not of the metered total. The shares deliberately do not sum to 1 — the gap is traffic on the direct hostname, which carries no consumer identity.

panels.title: Gateway latency p95, rolling 1h, by consumer
panels.description: Exact: summed in ClickHouse over SGLang's per-request records (engine.requests) and the gateway access log, scraped as gauges by job engine-usage; see clickhouse/engine-usage-metrics.sql. Each point is the exact p95 of successful chat and completions requests in the hour before it, as the gateway timed them (whole request).

panels.title: Status mix by consumer · $window
panels.description: Exact: summed in ClickHouse over SGLang's per-request records (engine.requests) and the gateway access log, scraped as gauges by job engine-usage; see clickhouse/engine-usage-metrics.sql. Exact counts from the gateway access log for the selected window. `unauthenticated` is the 401 path. cut = billable request that ended before its usage frame (client disconnect, timeout, upstream error) and was charged nothing.

panels.title: Exact usage by consumer · $window
panels.description: Exact: summed in ClickHouse over SGLang's per-request records (engine.requests) and the gateway access log, scraped as gauges by job engine-usage; see clickhouse/engine-usage-metrics.sql. Tokens are what the ledger charged (aborted requests excluded). cache hit = prompt tokens the engine did not recompute, over the input whose cache split was recorded; HiCache = the part reloaded from host RAM. Cached input is still charged in full. A high in : out means the bill is context re-sent, not work generated.

targets.expr: (sum by (consumer) (engine_usage_cached_device_tokens{consumer=~"$consumer", window="$window"}) + sum by (consumer) (engine_usage_cached_host_tokens{consumer=~"$consumer", window="$window"})) / (sum by (consumer) (engine_usage_cache_known_prompt_tokens{consumer=~"$consumer", window="$window"}) > 0)

panels.title: Engine TTFT p95, by consumer
panels.description: Time to first token as the ENGINE measured it: queue wait plus prefill, with no gateway, router or network in it. Histogram-based, so approximate at low request counts. Requests that did not come through the gateway carry consumer="" and are excluded here. The label arrives on x-request-id-labels, not SGLang's default x-custom-labels: the router forwards only an allow-list plus the x-request-id- prefix, so the default name is silently dropped. See docs/METRICS-ECOSYSTEM.md.

panels.title: Inter-token latency p95, by consumer
panels.description: Gap between successive output tokens, per consumer. Nothing else in the stack can produce this: the gateway sees a stream start and a stream end, so a request that stalls halfway through decode looks identical to one that flowed evenly. This is the metric the per-key work was for. Requests that did not come through the gateway carry consumer="" and are excluded here. The label arrives on x-request-id-labels, not SGLang's default x-custom-labels: the router forwards only an allow-list plus the x-request-id- prefix, so the default name is silently dropped. See docs/METRICS-ECOSYSTEM.md.

panels.title: Prefix cache hit, rolling 1h, by consumer
panels.description: Exact: summed in ClickHouse over SGLang's per-request records (engine.requests) and the gateway access log, scraped as gauges by job engine-usage; see clickhouse/engine-usage-metrics.sql. Each point: share of the consumer's prompt tokens in the preceding hour that the engine served from its prefix cache (all), and the part reloaded from host RAM (HiCache). A GPU hit is nearly free; a HiCache reload costs ~1.2 s per 45K tokens against ~14 s to recompute.

targets.expr: (sum by (consumer) (engine_usage_cached_device_tokens{consumer=~"$consumer", window="1h"}) + sum by (consumer) (engine_usage_cached_host_tokens{consumer=~"$consumer", window="1h"})) / (sum by (consumer) (engine_usage_cache_known_prompt_tokens{consumer=~"$consumer", window="1h"}) > 0)

panels.title: Output token rate, by consumer and replica
panels.description: Which GPU is doing whose work. The gateway cannot answer this — it hands every request to one router address and never learns which replica served it — so this is the only view that ties a consumer to r0 or r1, and the place a routing imbalance shows up per tenant. Requests that did not come through the gateway carry consumer="" and are excluded here. The label arrives on x-request-id-labels, not SGLang's default x-custom-labels: the router forwards only an allow-list plus the x-request-id- prefix, so the default name is silently dropped. See docs/METRICS-ECOSYSTEM.md.

panels.title: Gateway p95 minus engine p95, rolling 1h, by consumer
panels.description: Difference of two exact p95s over the same hour — still quantile arithmetic, not per-request overhead, and it can go negative. MEASURED TRUTH, from duration_ms - llm_ms per request in gateway.requests over 30 days: p50 1ms, p95 3ms, p99 7ms, max 14ms. The gateway filter chain costs single-digit milliseconds.

targets.expr: max by (consumer) (gateway_usage_duration_seconds{consumer=~"$consumer", p="95", window="1h"}) - max by (consumer) (engine_usage_e2e_seconds{consumer=~"$consumer", p="95", window="1h"})
